conf.description: Cribl Stream internal-logs (CriblLogs Worker Process feed): field selection/typing/ECS naming over already-flat JSON, event.action derived only for the two literal message tokens the work order actually names, epoch-second start/end window, cpuPerc normalized as far as the data allows.

conf.comment: cribl-internal/internal-logs/json. Records arrive as flat JSON, stable keys, no _raw to deserialize. message is a fixed discriminator, not prose; event.action derived only for the two literal tokens given ('_raw stats', 'Successful login') - 'a backpressure/pq notice' is not a literal string, so no token match invented for it. host.cpu.usage divided by 100 only - no core-count field exists to finish the ECS 0-1 normalization. mem.rss read tolerating either nested {mem:{rss}} or a literal flat dotted key (BIG ONE trap) since the wire form isn't stated. Must stay cheap/never throw - it observes its own telemetry.

functions.description: flat-JSON assumption, event.action scope, cpuPerc/core-count gap, mem.rss ambiguity

compute _time (never @timestamp, platform constraint), event.start/event.end tolerating the documented starttime/startTime casing inconsistency, host.cpu.usage's partial normalization, mem.rss's nested-or-flat tolerant read, and event.action/event.outcome for the two literal message tokens - all before rename

batch rename every clean-identifier mapped/unmapped field to its ECS or cribl.* custom target; message is already correctly named (ecs target is also 'message') so it is intentionally excluded from this batch as a no-op

event.dataset (no hyphen), cleanup of the raw window/timestamp/cpu originals fully consumed above - mem/mem.rss deliberately left in place (see comment: removing it correctly requires knowing which of the two representations is real, and an incorrect glob risks deleting sibling mem.* fields not in this work order's table)
Re-nest flat dotted keys (data-maps canonical step)
